companies.name: Zupee
companies.what_they_did: Built mobile versions of traditional Indian games like Ludo, Snakes and Ladders, and Carrom. Discontinued gaming operations and laid off its entire workforce.
companies.story: Founded in 2018, Zupee raised over $120 million and served over 200 million users with casual and real-money games. After a ban on real-money gaming damaged its revenue streams and portfolio failover, the startup announced an AI pivot that sources called a smokescreen. Ultimately, Zupee shut down its operations and laid off its entire workforce.
reasons: Ban on real-money gaming dealt a significant blow to revenue streams.
Existing portfolio of casual games failed to generate enough revenue.
AI pivot failed to materialize and served as a smoke screen for winding down.
companies.one_line: The ban on real-money gaming and failure of casual games to offset losses led to its shutdown.

causes.proof: Zupee s downfall began with the ban on real-money gaming (RMG), which dealt a significant blow to its revenue streams.
